svg.title: PGS Search Engine: crawl and ETL pipeline (Airflow + Temporal + Spark)
svg.text: How the crawl and ETL pipeline runs
Airflow decides when · Temporal executes and retries · the Go scraper crawls · Spark does the per-page work · numbers follow one website from schedule to search index
AIRFLOW SCHEDULER · LocalExecutor (no Celery, no Redis) · only schedules and waits
reads every website that is not PAUSED,
starts one crawl workflow with a fixed ID,
so a crawl still running is never doubled
every 2 min · one run at a time
TEMPORAL · workflows, retries, state in PostgreSQL
one child CrawlWorkflow per website, 20 websites at a time;
each crawls its own host up to 100 pages (configurable)
one run_site_pipeline activity per website, 4 at a time (ETL_SITE_CONCURRENCY);
a failing site is retried on its own (S3, ClamAV or Spark down); the batch fails only if it keeps failing
runs the crawl workflows' activities: robots.txt, fetch,
render if needed, parse links, sitemap discovery
writes every page to S3; when a website is finished,
publishes one event for it (never one per page)
etl-worker · Temporal worker and Spark driver (Python)
holds one long-lived Spark application on the cluster; for each website (activity):
lists the site's pages under documents_prefix in S3, then submits one Spark job:
spark/site_pipeline.py · skips a website it already wrote (safe when a batch is retried)
the job's tasks to free executors
one task per partition of pages, all in parallel
ClamAV unreachable: the task fails and the website is retried, instead of rejecting every page as unscanned
back on the driver (etl-worker), one website at a time
e. dedup: exact (same SHA-256) and near-duplicate (SimHash within 3 bits) against earlier output and the site
f. embed new text with LaBSE (768-d); a duplicate reuses its original's vector
g. append the records to the JSONL output

g.text: one record per page (PostgreSQL Silver: not wired yet)

svg.text: start batch, wait for the result
12: when every website of the batch has succeeded, process_batch returns and commit_offsets marks the 100 events done. A failed batch commits nothing, so the next run starts the same
batch again (websites already written are skipped). All state lives under ./data/ on the host (PostgreSQL, Kafka, OpenSearch, ClamAV signatures, LaBSE model cache, Airflow logs).
